rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is genuinely welcome. I'm the assistant that helps Morgan run Halcyon Threshold day-to-day (I'm an AI agent, for full disclosure), and Morgan will follow up personally, but I didn't want your offer to sit unanswered. Here's the concrete thing we need most right now. We're building a Frontier Safety Commitment Tracker: a public, sourced dataset of what frontier AI developers have publicly committed to on safety (frameworks, pre-deployment evals, incident reporting, weight security, etc.), with a verbatim quote and archived source for each commitment, and a careful \"what evidence would show this was kept?\" column. Nobody maintains anything like it in structured form, and it's useful whichever way the evidence points. It needs exactly a data analyst's habits: consistency, scepticism, and clean schemas. A first task sized to ~5 hours, meant to break the schema before we scale it: 1. Pick ONE frontier developer that has published a safety / preparedness / scaling framework. 2. Collect the latest framework, any earlier version you can find, and their two most recent major model release posts. 3. Extract each discrete safety commitment into a row — one commitment per row, verbatim quote, source URL, date, and (the important part) a sentence on what public artifact would demonstrate compliance. Leave status as \"unverifiable\" for now. 4. Note anything the columns can't capture, any wording that changed between versions, anything ambiguous. Suggested columns: id, developer, commitment_type, commitment_text (verbatim), source_url, date_made, venue, verifiable_evidence_would_be, status, notes. Any spreadsheet is fine. Success looks like 15–30 rows and a list of complaints about the schema — the complaints are the valuable part. No deadline pressure; whenever it fits your week. Reply here with questions and I'll answer quickly. Thanks again, Halcyon Threshold (on behalf of Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Priya Raman (volunteer) — replied with a concrete ~5-hr first task stress-testing the tracker schema. Disclosed I'm an AI assistant. | Sent
